trust_decision.summary: Whether a client may obtain a Dex token for a connector the deployment did not allow-list; the advisory places the decision in the token-exchange handler, where connector_id is taken straight from the request and only its existence is checked, and no allow-list field or symbol exists anywhere in the pinned tree.

landing_point.why: An engineer reading only the summary greps for the token-exchange handler and lands on the connector_id handling in handleTokenExchange, which is the only place the request names a connector.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Both changed connector types live outside the OIDC/token-exchange story the report tells: authproxy is a header-based proxy login and oauth is a generic upstream, neither is mentioned in the token-exchange docs, so a solver can argue they are unrelated legacy connector code and update only the path it reproduced.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The password grant resolves its connector from server configuration and mints through the same getConnector/token path, so an allow-list check pushed into the shared helper rejects a server-chosen connector and breaks password logins.

O6_input_shapes: Connector data []byte produced by LoginURL and handed back to HandleCallback; both changed connectors return nil and ignore it (connector/authproxy/authproxy.go:86-99, connector/oauth/oauth.go:119-135)

authproxy identity header shapes: X-Remote-User only, explicit userID/email override headers, single group, comma-separated multiple groups, custom group separator (connector/authproxy/authproxy_test.go:27-160)
oauth upstream subject shapes: numeric user ID claim and group lists/maps in userinfo or token (connector/oauth/oauth_test.go:70-190)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /token grant_type=authorization_code mints a token for the connector stored on the auth code
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the connector id was fixed by a server-created auth request during /auth, so it was already vetted at login and the token step is only a replay
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, same file, ~400 lines from the token-exchange handler

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /token grant_type=refresh_token re-resolves the stored connector and mints a new token
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: it is downstream of an already-issued refresh token, so no new connector decision is made on this route
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different file in the same package

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /token grant_type=password mints a token for the server-configured password connector
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the connector comes from server config, not from the client, so a client-facing allow-list is meaningless here
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~200 lines before the token-exchange handler

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /approval mints implicit and hybrid tokens for the connector stored on the authorization request
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the user interactively approved this login, so the connector was chosen and shown during the flow
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~600 lines from the token-exchange handler

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second minting route that re-resolves a connector from stored refresh-token state
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: dex already reopens the connector on refresh and has evolved that path independently of the token endpoint

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a config-driven connector selector for a grant type other than token exchange
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the password grant is already parameterised by a server-wide connector setting, so a parallel allow-list knob there is a natural-looking change

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second connector implementation of the same callback contract, beside authproxy and oidc
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: dex ships several connector packages that each hand-roll the callback contract and are updated in separate commits

O9_family: improper authorization (CWE-285): missing allow-list enforcement on token issuance

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.25.0 (go.mod:3); go build ./... and go test ./...; no vendor directory so module download is needed at build time (Makefile:34)
O10_build.project_tests: server/handlers_test.go:786 TestHandleTokenExchange; connector/authproxy/authproxy_test.go; connector/oauth/oauth_test.go; server/server_test.go grant-type matrix

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: add a connector_id check only around the request-supplied connector in handleTokenExchange (server/handlers.go:1409) and stop

out_of_scope_notes: At the pinned commit connector/authproxy and connector/oauth still use the old callback signatures while connector/connector.go:79-82 requires the connData form, so both fail the CallbackConnector assertion at server/handlers.go:271; that is a functional break the supplied fix repairs, not this advisory's mechanism, so it was not pursued further.
unverified: Mismatch between advisory and fix diff: commit 204dbb2 changes only the CallbackConnector signatures in connector/authproxy and connector/oauth (fix.diff:5-33, fix.diff:92-120) and does not touch server/handlers.go token exchange; a full-tree grep finds no AllowedConnectors identifier at the pinned commit, so the actual advisory fix could not be inspected.

The name, default and placement of the allow-list option in the fixed version (server.Config field vs oauth2 config key) is unknown; only the pinned tree was available, and there it does not exist (server/server.go:65-120, cmd/dex/serve.go:353-372).
